chunks: Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Farqad, from Abū Kahmash, from ʿAbd al-Muʾmin al-Anṣārī, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Be ashamed of Allah with true shame.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is [considered to be] ashamed of Allah with true shame?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever wants to be ashamed of Allah with true shame, let him keep his death before his eyes, be abstemious in this world and its embellishments, protect the head and all that it contains [senses], and the stomach and all that it holds [food], and let him not forget the graves and the ruins [of decay].'

key_terms.الرَّأْسُ وَمَا حَوَى: The head and what it contains (referring to the senses and intellect)
key_terms.الزَّهْدُ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: Death or the appointed time of death
key_terms.الْبَطْنُ وَمَا طَوَى: The stomach and what it holds (referring to food and digestion)
key_terms.الْبَلَى: Ruins or decay, symbolizing the transient nature of the world
key_terms.حَقَّ الْحَيَاءِ: True shame or genuine modesty before God

ai.seo_question: What are the practical signs of having true shame (ḥaqqa l-ḥayāʾ) before God according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, outlines the practical dimensions of *al- haya'* (modesty/shame) as a spiritual discipline, linking internal consciousness of God to external ascetic practices. It emphasizes the 'death between the eyes' as a catalyst for detaching from worldly adornments and guarding the 'vessels' of the body (head and stomach), a concept central to Shia ethical theology regarding the purification of the self (*tazkiyah*).
